Developers of Astra Linux violate GPL, Microsoft Fonts Licence and Debian Trademark

Their APT repository does contain the source code of at least some packages. Bundling proprietary software with a Linux distro is not a new thing and a blanket license making the entire product proprietary also isn't (e.g. Red Hat and Ubuntu do that too). Such a license can't prevent you from unbundling individual components and using them according to their specific licenses.

So, although the Russian military (or any other military for that matter) can be negligent when it comes to fulfilling their duties as per the GPL, these people at least try to. If you want to accuse them of a GPL violation, you have to be more specific. Find a specific package and show how its license is being violated.

Fellow gators, I want to talk to you about very serious meta-problem that hits every large reddit community and by similarity of design may start bothering this subverse too if it will grow big enough. Recent drama surrounding falseflagging on ggrevolt have showed it in all gory details:

http://postimg.org/image/t8ava9v6h/

This widely known problem is called "Knights of New". By default subreddit/subverse shows HOT submissions. When community is small, this is not so bad, because slow pace makes new submissions appear somewhere at the bottom of HOT's first page even before voting starts. But when community grows larger, new submission appear only on NEW listing and are moving to first page of HOT if upvoted high enough. And here reality starts biting community's ass - overwhelming majority of subscribers simply do not check anything but default page. Tiny minority of people who are dedicated enough to click on NEW button are gaining huge power over what others see and what not - any topic that Knights of New consider problematic can be controllably downvoted into oblivion before having any chance to be seen by other subscribers. Such power is comparable to moderator's by magnitude, but comes with zero responsibility, because of anonymous voting process - this is making it enormously attractive to people with "gatekeeper" mentality. I think some preventative measures should be taken to avoid this cancer. Possible solutions coming on my mind:

  1. Changing default page of subverse to NEW instead of HOT - this solution has major downside, because same people who are too lazy to click NEW will be too lazy to click HOT and good topics may start falling into oblivion faster then deserved.

  2. Bureaucratic solution - we can make formally stated moderator's duty to overlook Knights of New and sticky every actively discussed submission that show signs of organised downvoting. This have downsides too, because even in good case of responsible moderators it defeats Knights of New only in high-profile cases, when post can generate discussion even before appearing on HOT.

  3. Simply disabling downvote button for submissions. Organised upvoting of posts is much less dangerous and make weak weapon for Knights of New.

  4. Asking Voat administration for a new feature - BUMP sorting order, that lists most recently commented submissions, forum-style. Making such sorting order default for subverse would probably be the best solution, as I do not see any downsides, but requirement of new feature from Voat itself makes it most hard to implement too.

Share your thoughts and proposals, please - we need to think for the future, as reddit may go crazy any moment already.
